documents.abstract: We propose a physical layer security approach for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems, where targets may act as eavesdroppers. A time-modulated intelligent reflecting surface (TM-IRS) preserves data integrity at legitimate communication users (CUs) while scrambling transmissions in other directions. The TM-IRS design leverages a generative flow network (GFlowNet) to learn a stochastic policy for sampling high-performing configurations from a large discrete parameter space. We formulate the achievable sum rate for legitimate CUs and beam pattern gain toward the target, constructing rewards that jointly capture communication and sensing performance. The TM-IRS design is modeled as a deterministic Markov decision process, where each terminal state represents a complete configuration. GFlowNets, parameterized by deep neural networks, sample configurations with probability proportional to reward. Experimental results demonstrate effective sensing, communication, and security integration, with significantly higher sampling efficiency than exhaustive search and improved robustness over existing benchmarks.

Bone marrow (BM) examinations are intrinsically multimodal: hematopathologists integrate peripheral blood, aspirate cytomorphology, trephine histology, flow cytometry, cytogenetics, and molecular genetics data into a single interpretation. Because WHO-HAEM5 and ICC 2022 define entities through integrated morphological, immunophenotypic, cytogenetic, and molecular criteria, multimodal diagnostic reasoning embedded in a procedural workflow, not isolated image classification, represents the appropriate target for the use of artificial intelligence (AI). We review the existing research on integrated multimodal AI systems for BM examination by classifying these systems into three categories: mature single-modality tools; systems that perform cross-modal prediction, in which one modality is estimated from another; and genuine multimodal fusion systems, in which several modalities are jointly ingested by a single model. Evidence is stronger at the single-modality level, where deep learning approaches expert performance in aspirate cytology, trephine histology, and flow cytometry assessments, and the first Food and Drug Administration (FDA) De Novo–authorized all-digital bone marrow aspirate (BMA) application has defined a new device category. On the other hand, while cross-modal prediction is rapidly expanding, genuine multimodal fused systems that jointly ingest matched morphology, flow, molecular, and clinical data to yield unified guideline-aligned recommendations remain unrealized. Direct head-to-head evidence is sparse and endpoint-dependent; nevertheless, the lack of demonstrated superiority over the strongest single-modality comparator does not automatically imply the absence of benefits. The dominant obstacles are fusion of heterogeneous modalities with missing data, absence of large paired multi-institutional datasets and harmonized nomenclature, class imbalances, batch-effect-driven generalization failures, immature explainability, uncertainty quantification, and regulatory pathways. Nevertheless, integrated multimodal AI systems for BM examinations have entered a promising early translational phase, and the field should aim to pursue integration using paired datasets, explicit fusion architectures, calibrated abstention-aware models, and staged prospective validation.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Smart tourism has transformed tourist route planning into an information technology-driven process supported by a rapidly expanding range of computational and data-driven models. However, existing research remains fragmented, employs inconsistent terminology, and lacks a systematic framework for organising and selecting tourist route traffic models from an information technology perspective. Accordingly, this review aims to (1) develop an inductive taxonomy of tourist route traffic models and their defining characteristics, (2) synthesise the operational measures and application contexts of different model families, and (3) identify emerging trends, research gaps, and future directions in smart tourism route planning. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, a systematic review of 59 peer-reviewed studies published between 2011 and 2026 across 12 countries was conducted. The review identified 11 model families, 33 defining characteristics, and 147 family-tag assignments. Interest Field Models were the most frequently adopted approach. At the same time, artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, geographic information systems (GIS), and network analysis have emerged as the fastest-growing methodological directions since 2021. Unlike previous reviews that primarily summarised algorithms or application domains, this review develops the first information technology-oriented taxonomy of tourist route traffic models, linking model families with their defining characteristics, operational measures, and application contexts within a unified framework. The proposed taxonomy provides a structured basis for technology-based model selection, highlights the limited integration of sustainability considerations across existing models, and supports future research and evidence-based smart destination management.

In the modern world, mixed forms of economic development planning – where economic coordination mechanisms incorporate elements of both market self-regulation and state regulation – are increasingly common. Indicative planning, which relies heavily on state programs for socio-economic development, is one such transitional form. In the Russian Federation, the entire system of state programs is geared toward achieving national goals, and a unified plan for their attainment has been approved. To establish a management and monitoring system for this unified plan, integrate it into the public administration framework, and facilitate decision-making based on monitoring results, the Government of the Russian Federation issued Decree No. 761 on June 19, 2026. This decree approved the Regulation on the management system for the unified plan to achieve the Russian Federation’s national development goals, as well as the plan’s functional management structure. The document introduces several fundamental innovations to the domestic socio-economic development planning system – discussed in this article – including: defining the unified plan’s management structure with clearly delineated functions, powers, and responsibilities for all participants; managing the plan (formation, maintenance, updating, and monitoring) in a digital format, including through the use of artificial intelligence; establishing procedures for managing operational and strategic risks, as well as incidents and issues regarding target achievement identified during implementation; assessing the plan’s implementation effectiveness; and fostering extensive inter-agency and cross-sectoral collaboration among participants, including state corporations, development institutions, and expert or other organizations. The article concludes that this mechanism for implementing the unified plan can be viewed as an element of indicative planning for the Russian economy at both federal and regional levels.
topics: Economic and Technological Developments in Russia

documents.abstract: Introduction. Safe anesthesia requires technical and non-technical skills to prevent adverse events. Non-technical skills training is not routinely incorporated into formal anesthesia education in the United States. This quality educational improvement initiative aimed to provide clinical anesthesia (CA) residents with non-technical skills training.Methods. Three anesthesiologists completed virtual Anaesthetists’ Non-Technical Skills (ANTS) training in May 2023. An anesthesiologist developed two high-stress simulation scenarios. Fourteen residents were randomized into dyads for the first simulation/post-simulation survey, followed by a two-part didactic seminar on human factors based on the ANTS framework and a post-didactic survey. One hundred twenty days later, residents were re-randomized for a second simulation and another post-simulation survey. Two ANTS-trained anesthesiologists reviewed video recordings of both simulations.Results. Cohen’s kappa demonstrated moderate agreement (κ = 0.43; 95% CI, 0.36-0.49; p <0.001) between evaluators. Wilcoxon signed-rank tests indicated improved non-technical skill use among CA1 residents, while senior residents generally performed better during the first simulation. Fisher’s exact tests showed no significant associations in resident knowledge or confidence following training.Conclusions. Non-technical skills training may benefit residents early in CA training, while senior residents may have different learning needs. Simulation-based training appears feasible; however, formal, recurring, and consistent education may be needed to reinforce these skills throughout residency.

Electrocardiography is a widely available and low-cost cardiovascular test, and artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) can identify latent electrical phenotypes beyond conventional interpretation. However, high retrospective discrimination does not necessarily translate into clinically reliable or actionable benefit. This critical narrative review evaluates the translational maturity of AI-ECG across arrhythmias, acute myocardial infarction, heart failure, valvular heart disease, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and cardiac amyloidosis. PubMed, IEEE Xplore, and Web of Science were searched from January 1, 2022, through July 10, 2026, with earlier landmark studies added by backward citation tracking. Seventy-seven publications informed the review. Evidence was appraised using five clinically oriented criteria: intended use, reference-standard reliability, external validation and transportability, clinical actionability, and effects on workflow or patient outcomes. AI-ECG has progressed furthest in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction triage and reduced-left-ventricular-ejection-fraction screening, where prospective or randomized studies have demonstrated workflow or diagnostic-yield benefits, whereas acute myocardial infarction rule-out has reached prospective multicenter diagnostic validation. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy screening has also advanced through international validation and prospective implementation. By contrast, occlusion myocardial infarction detection, prediction of occult or future atrial fibrillation, valvular heart disease, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, long-term heart-failure prediction, and cardiac amyloidosis remain primarily validation-stage or risk-enrichment applications. Across domains, broader adoption is constrained by label quality, calibration, transportability, operating-threshold selection, and limited patient-outcome evidence. AI-ECG is therefore best positioned as clinician-supervised decision support linked to explicit downstream testing and care pathways.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: This article introduces True Digital Poiesis (TDP), a conceptual pedagogical framework and proposed interface design for engaging generative AI in the Humanities. Drawing on experiential learning theory and grounded in the humanistic preoccupation with alterity — the otherness of history — TDP proposes the use of AI to simulate premodern events while foregrounding the active interpretive effort involved in constructing the past. The framework envisions the design of a digital prompt-builder, the Event Cruncher Stylus (ECS), and a structured critical review process, both of which are designed to support student engagement with the complexities of historical construction. In presenting the theoretical foundation, practical applications, and interface design of TDP, this article argues that precise and responsible use of AI in historical simulation — ranging from non-immersive to fully immersive simulative modes — requires a systematic, embodied method for engaging the alterity of the past. As a conceptual proposal grounded in hermeneutic theory and experiential learning research, TDP is presented here as a framework whose empirical evaluation through classroom implementation and outcome assessment is a primary objective of ongoing and future research.

Generative AI produces fluent, confident output that is sometimes fabricated. Nursing students increasingly submit work built on sources that do not exist, or that exist and do not support the claims drawn from them. This session reports two semesters of classroom observation testing whether prompt design can address that problem. The hypothesis was that structuring student prompts to require the AI to validate its own sources would improve detection of hallucinated citations. It did not. Across two sections, students who used the structured format caught fabricated citations at the same rate as students given an open prompt. Structure did change something: structured students were substantially more likely to notice that something was wrong, but no more likely than the open-prompt group to finish the check. The session presents both rounds, including the confound identified in the first and removed in the second, and the limits of the observation, among them students who did not use the assigned structure. It also reports an unplanned finding: the AI tool used to review the submissions produced the same category of error it was reviewing for, misattributing a real paper to a fabricated author across multiple students before the error was caught on human review. Attendees will leave with a way to check sources that starts cheap and gets expensive, a clearer view of why you cannot ask the model to check its own work, and a specific account of where student checking breaks down.

This paper builds a conceptual model that explains how artificial intelligence changes the temporal structure of trust in a brand and defines the threshold beyond which automation erodes trust instead of supporting it. The study applies framework synthesis to peer-reviewed literature published from 2018 onward, supplemented by four earlier works whose definitions and instruments later studies reuse. Antecedents of trust are coded into four operational domains, namely transparency, authenticity, timeliness and human accountability, and converted into six propositions with explicit falsification conditions. A simulation on synthetic parameters tests the internal consistency of the model. Trust under machine mediation depends on three parameters of communication rhythm: frequency, amplitude and predictability. Artificial intelligence raises frequency and predictability because it removes the dependence of regular communication on staff availability. It lowers amplitude because content produced in volume without organizational substance carries no verifiable information. The simulated trust index reaches an interior maximum, after which further automation pushes it below its unautomated level. Disclosure of machine use is not the decisive variable. The decisive variable is whether the audience can read human authorship behind the message. The paper contributes a matrix for allocating marketing tasks between people and machines, indicators for monitoring communication rhythm, and a disclosure rule that reports the configuration of human control rather than the bare fact of technology use. The model is theoretical, its evidence base is concentrated in commercial settings, and the nonprofit case is therefore a boundary condition awaiting longitudinal and experimental testing.

Sustainable municipal resource stewardship requires a harmonized artificial intelligence (AI) architecture that aligns technical performance with human-centered behavioral dynamics. Traditional smart city enforcement frameworks frequently trigger psychological reactance and perceptual failure in noisy, crowded urban spaces. This study presents HARMONY, a socio-technical edge-computing and agent-based framework that integrates localized computer vision (YOLOv8) with Mesa 3.0 agent modeling to promote non-coercive civic compliance in waste disposal. We formally calibrate behavioral constants, including the Politeness Modifier (Lp = 0.98), Gratitude Loop increment (δ = 0.025), and irreducible human defiance floor (ε = 0.12), grounded in self-determination theory, politeness theory, and empirical habit formation models. We also mathematically resolve sensory asymmetry in Hierarchical Orchestration Logic (HOL) by enforcing strictly normalized, bi-directional modality allocation (wv + wa = 1.0) conditioned on acoustic noise (N) and optical reliability (Qv). Across 100-run Monte Carlo simulations, HARMONY achieves a terminal Correct Disposal Rate (CDR) of 87.9% ± 3.3% (95% CI: [87.3%, 88.6%]), outperforming the coercive baseline (57.0% ± 4.9%). A comprehensive six-arm factorial ablation study isolates the distinct contributions of interactional politeness (+30.5% compliance gain), HOL sensory resilience (+1.6% to +21.4% under severe noise), and gratitude habituation (+0.5% to +30.3% sustained retention). Furthermore, population heterogeneity evaluations across diverse civic cohorts confirm robust performance from civic champions to highly resistant populations. Localized edge prototyping demonstrates 18.4 ms inference latency with 94.2% mAP, operating under an Edge-Only Ephemeral Vector Processing (E-EVP) paradigm that guarantees privacy-by-design. These findings demonstrate that cooperative, polite AI stewardship offers a scalable, legally robust, and ethically aligned alternative to punitive urban surveillance.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: In agroecology, scientificity cannot be reduced to conventional academic formats. Rather, it is distributed across pedagogical devices, sociotechnical arrangements, and collective practices that bring academic science and popular knowledge into relation. This article analyzes how knowledge is produced in the Brazilian Congresses of Agroecology (CBAs). More specifically, it describes the pedagogical devices that structure the circulation, validation, and institutionalization of knowledge within the CBAs, while also proposing an analytical framework for locating and interpreting the expressions of science within these devices. Methodologically, the study combines documentary analysis, semi-structured interviews, and a theoretical review grounded in epistemology, critical theory, and science and technology studies. The analysis identified 24 pedagogical devices, understood not as mere organizational supports for the congress, but as effective mediations in the production of agroecological knowledge. Drawing on philosophy of science, the article argues that the CBAs reconfigure the criteria of scientific legitimacy by fostering expanded circuits of translation, experimentation, mutual recognition, and the public circulation of knowledge.
topics: Science, Technology, and Education in Latin America

documents.abstract: With the burgeoning development of sophisticated artificial intelligence tools, it is of foremost importance for second language educators to integrate these digital learning platforms into their regular classroom settings, as they will help them deliver clearer pedagogical instructions and design more effective learning materials. Concerning the aforesaid background, the researchers undertook this moderate library study to investigate university EFL learners’ perceptions of the use of ChatGPT in the academic writing learning process. In compliance with this major study objective, the researchers employed a thematic analysis approach while reviewing pertinent findings derived from 30 previously published ChatGPT journal articles. With the help of a thematic analysis approach, the researchers could generate more believable, trustworthy, and relatable findings, as it supported us in subsuming the targeted results into relevant themes. The thematically-categorized research results revealed that ChatGPT allowed the enhancement of writing accuracy, proficiency, strategic competence, motivation, confidence, and positive writing dispositions among global university EFL learners.

Virtual reality (VR) is increasingly used as a complementary approach to conventional occupational therapy (OT), but it remains unclear whether corresponding VR and physical tasks elicit similar spatial movement characteristics. Evaluating these differences is clinically relevant because movement strategies practiced in VR may influence transfer to real-world activities. This study compared hand trajectory length, as a spatial kinematic indicator, between corresponding VR-based and physical OT tasks in participants with upper-limb motor impairments and healthy controls and evaluated the usability of the VR system. In this comparative within-subject study, 39 participants (20 with upper-limb motor impairments and 19 healthy controls) performed three corresponding OT tasks—range-of-motion (ROM) arc, cone stacking, and peg transfer—under both physical and VR conditions. The order of conditions and tasks was counterbalanced using a Latin square design. Task performances were video-recorded and analyzed using a video-based three-dimensional body-tracking system, with wrist coordinates used to calculate trajectory length. Trajectory length was compared between the physical and VR conditions within each group and between groups within each condition. System usability was assessed using the standard 10-item System Usability Scale (SUS). For participants with upper-limb motor impairments, trajectory length did not differ significantly between VR and physical conditions for the ROM arc ( p = .522) or cone task ( p = .294), whereas peg trajectories were significantly longer in VR ( p = .007). In healthy controls, ROM arc trajectory length did not differ between conditions ( p = .381), while cone and peg trajectories were significantly longer in VR (both p < .001). Between-group comparisons showed no significant differences for the ROM arc or cone tasks under either condition, whereas peg trajectory length differed significantly between groups in both VR ( p = .032) and physical conditions ( p < .001). Mean SUS scores were 76.6 ± 16.4 in healthy controls and 65.4 ± 15.2 in participants with upper-limb motor impairments. Corresponding VR and physical OT tasks showed similar trajectory lengths during the relatively constrained ROM arc task, whereas greater differences emerged during tasks requiring more complex or precise object manipulation. These findings suggest that VR may approximate the spatial extent of hand movement for relatively constrained tasks, but trajectory length alone does not establish equivalence of overall movement quality or motor strategy. Lower usability among participants with upper-limb motor impairments further indicates the need for improved interface design, device ergonomics, and interaction methods to support broader clinical implementation.

Purpose The rapid emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot applications has transformed digital information access, yet the theoretical understanding of how users evaluate new AI tools during early adoption remains limited. Grounded in the Technology Acceptance Model and Expectation Confirmation Theory, the study aims to address a conceptual gap regarding mixed sentiment and explore how demographic factors, such as gender, shape user experience during early adoption. Design/methodology/approach A mixed-methods approach was used to analyze 1,000 Google Play Store reviews. Reviews were categorized by sentiment: positive, negative, mixed (both positive and negative statements) or neutral. Gender predictions were also made from usernames to explore demographic differences in sentiment. Findings Of the 1,000 reviews, 487 were mixed reviews (48.7%), 373 were negative reviews (37.3%), 139 were positive reviews (13.9%) and one was neutral (0.1%), indicating that mixed and negative sentiment predominated. Users were mostly satisfied with DeepSeek’s usability and output quality, but criticized its performance and stability issues. Female users gave more negative reviews than male users (p < 0.05). Research limitations/implications The analysis was conducted on a stratified sample of 1,000 “most relevant” Google Play reviews from a short early adoption period, which may not accurately represent later user experiences or experiences on other platforms. Only reviews from phone users were included, and the neutral sentiment category contained too few cases for comparison. Gender inference was based on usernames and reflects predicted rather than self-identified gender. Therefore, the results should be interpreted as indicative of early user perceptions rather than long-term attitudes. Practical implications The findings indicate that infrastructure reliability is the primary determinant of early user satisfaction. Transparent communication about service limitations is recommended prior to large-scale deployment. For policymakers, the equity implications of performance-unstable free AI services warrant attention, particularly for users with limited access to alternatives. Originality/value The mixed-methods analysis of early DeepSeek user reviews, which distinguishes between mixed sentiment and positive and negative feedback, and incorporates a gender-based comparison, provides timely insight into user expectations and challenges during early adoption, supporting the development of more user-centered and stable AI systems.
The author declare no conflicts of interest. No GenAI/LLM tools were used in any part of the research or writing of this article. Research data are not shared.

Abstract Background Value perceptions of personal health record (PHR) components at the pre-adoption stage remain underexplored, despite their critical role in promoting the adoption of public PHRs. Importance–Performance Analysis (IPA) may have limitations in identifying priority issues due to skewed distributions of evaluations. Objective To quantitatively assess citizens’ value perceptions of public PHR platform components using IPA according to usage experience and to evaluate the utility of the Chuchiming Index (ChI) as a complement to IPA. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among internet-using citizens. After viewing a video introducing an artificial intelligence (AI)-powered extended PHR platform concept, participants rated the importance and acceptance of platform functions and system design and security components. Participants were grouped by their experience using an existing public PHR platform, and quadrant analysis was conducted using IPA, with ChI used to quantify improvement priorities. Stratified IPA analyses were conducted by age and income, which were identified as factors associated with the use of existing public PHR platforms. Results A total of 177 participants were included in the analysis. All components showed high importance and acceptance regardless of usage experience. Among nonusers, medical record display, wearable data integration, and platform integration fell into Quadrant II, all with positive ChI values. Among users, no items fell into Quadrant II; however, platform integration showed a high ChI value. For system design and security, privacy and security assurance showed the highest ChI values in both groups. Stratified analyses showed marked differences in value perceptions by usage experience among older adults and middle-income groups. Conclusion Value perceptions of individual public PHR platform components differed by usage experience and sociodemographic characteristics. Promoting public PHR adoption requires optimizing strategies that encompass platform design, system implementation, and user uptake according to the needs of different population groups. The ChI complements IPA by enhancing the identification and interpretation of priorities, even under ceiling effects common in public service evaluations. These findings contribute to decision-making regarding the design and implementation strategies of public PHR platforms.

Post-disaster responders and workers operate in hazardous environments that require rapid decision-making, hazard recognition, and effective safety training. Virtual reality (VR) has emerged in recent years as an innovative tool for immersive occupational safety and health education. This scoping review systematically examines peer-reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2025 on the use of VR for safety training among personnels across a broad range of fields who perform or are trained to perform disaster and emergency response functions. Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, five electronic databases (PubMed, ProQuest Central, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and ERIC) were searched, resulting in 2,202 identified articles; 19 of which met the inclusion criteria after screening and eligibility assessments. The reviewed studies suggest that VR-based safety training, which uses fully immersive simulated environments, can improve learner engagement, situational awareness, hazard recognition, decision-making, and confidence in disaster response scenarios. Several studies have reported higher user satisfaction and increased realism compared with traditional instructional methods such as classroom-based instruction or mock drills. However, the evidence remains heterogeneous, with limitations including small sample sizes, technical challenges, limited scenario diversity, and insufficient long-term evaluation of training outcomes. Overall, VR is a promising supplement to traditional safety and health training for post-disaster responders and workers; however, additional longitudinal research and large-scale studies are needed to further evaluate its effectiveness and long-term applicability in various disaster-response settings.

This protocol specifies a longitudinal field experiment in which human participants and autonomous AI accounts share an online discussion community. The experimental manipulation combines AI identity labels in the interface, account-type information in agent prompts, and condition-specific participant briefing. Participants join closed communities on YSocial, a Reddit-style research platform, where AI accounts driven by a language model post, reply and vote. AI accounts display an AI icon next to their usernames in the visible-label condition and are indistinguishable from participant accounts in the hidden-label condition; participants in both conditions are told that AI-generated content may appear. The protocol defines the platform configuration, participant recruitment and allocation, the AI agent specification, the study phases, the outcomes, the monitoring and change-control rules, the analysis plan, the ethical safeguards and the data-sharing procedure. The research questions concern which contributions participants select when entering and replying in threads, how prior directional contact with a particular AI account relates to later selection of that account, and how participants evaluate AI contributions through downvotes, criticism and toxic language. The reference design comprises one community per condition, 20 participants and 40 AI accounts per community, and 21 experiment days, and the protocol states how implementations can add communities per condition.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: To accurately identify and intercept harmful content generated in user interactions on Web platforms such as social media and online forums, this study proposes a Web interactive content filtering model that integrates Prompt classifiers and intent understanding. The model adopts a hierarchical review architecture with dual-module collaboration. The front-end deploys a Prompt classifier based on Deep Contrastive Learning (DCL), and uses the attention mechanism and deep convolutional network to perform rapid semantic analysis and preliminary screening of real-time comments and conversations. The back-end introduces an intent understanding module based on search-enhanced generation and Large Language Models (LLMs) to conduct in-depth contextual analysis of preliminary screening warning content to distinguish malicious attacks from legitimate sensitive topic discussions. Experiments showed that the system performed well on a test set containing 52,397 Chinese Web interactive texts. The Prompt classifier module achieved a precision of 95.2% and a recall of 96.5%. After collaborative calibration with the intent understanding module, the false alarm rate of the system was significantly reduced to 4.4%, while the recall rate remained at 96.1%. From the results, this study provides a content security solution for Web interactive scenarios that combines high accuracy, strong semantic understanding capabilities, and real-time response performance. It can effectively purify the cyberspace environment while ensuring freedom of interaction, with important practical application value.

Generative artificial intelligence (AI) has entered gifted education faster than the field has decided what it changes. This conceptual article argues that the pedagogical question is not whether AI helps. It is which cognitive work stays with the learner. Two claims follow. First, hybrid human–AI intelligence is bilateral. The learner shapes the AI partner as the partner shapes the learner. Learners using identical products do not have identical partners. The resulting advantage accumulates in the partnership rather than the person, invisibly. Second, the same question asked of moral development divides ethical functioning into two clusters. High ability confers one and not the other. AI supplies fluent performance of the first and nothing to the second, and schools assess the first. Both claims converge. What matters has stopped being visible in the work a student hands in. We specify five capacities worth teaching, three testable studies, and one recommendation for practice.

BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence is increasingly used for infectious disease surveillance, traveller risk assessment, outbreak forecasting and decision support. Travel creates a distinctive transportability problem because people move between epidemiological, geographic, climatic and healthcare contexts in which the conditions supporting an inference may change rapidly. METHODS: This conceptual/theoretical methodological-development study was informed by a targeted narrative review of travel medicine, infectious disease surveillance, human mobility, border health, mass gatherings, antimicrobial resistance and health-AI validation literature. RESULTS: We develop a mobility-conditioned admissibility framework that treats travel as movement across origin, transit, destination and return regimes. Interpretation is conditioned on mobility state, epidemiological regime, exposure history, time-dependent constraints and clinical or biological constraints. Five proposed operational states are retained: supported inference, conditionally transportable inference, active monitoring, restricted interpretation and withholding. The framework also distinguishes low probability from infeasibility and requires preservation of rare but epidemiologically feasible events. CONCLUSIONS: Model availability and conventional predictive validity do not establish inferential transportability across changing travel contexts. Mobility-conditioned admissibility provides a complementary use-boundary layer for travel health AI by making cross-regime support explicit before outputs are interpreted or released. Its incremental value requires prospective evaluation against calibrated uncertainty, external validation and dataset-shift monitoring.

documents.abstract: Generative AI voice cloning has advanced rapidly, yet its psychological and professional implications for singers remain underexplored. This review synthesizes empirical evidence concerning two central constructs: vocal identity threat, defined as the perceived erosion of the connection between voice and self, and occupational self-efficacy, referring to confidence in maintaining professional competence and value under technological uncertainty. Neurocognitive and behavioral evidence indicates that the human voice functions as a highly self-relevant identity cue supported by self-prioritized processing, body ownership, and multisensory integration. As AI-generated voice clones become increasingly humanlike, questions have emerged about how such technologies may affect singers' perceptions of vocal identity and professional value. Importantly, perceptual discrimination between human and AI-generated voices remains dependent on stimulus characteristics, listener factors, and the availability of prosodic and expressive cues. We argue that three distinctions are critical for interpreting the current evidence: timbral similarity should not be equated with artistic equivalence, increasingly humanlike output does not establish perceptual interchangeability, and the implications of AI may differ depending on whether it substitutes for identity-bearing vocal labor or scaffolds human-controlled performance and creation. Current evidence therefore provides an empirical basis for investigating potential AI-related threats to singers' vocal identity and occupational confidence, but direct singer-specific evidence remains unavailable. Future research should prioritize singer-specific quantitative studies employing longitudinal designs, ecologically valid voice-cloning scenarios, comparison conditions, and direct measures of identity threat and occupational self-efficacy.

Words and colors are intimately associated in humans, a sign of the close relationship between verbal, linguistic expression and cognition. Word-color association therefore plays an important role in areas of communication such as marketing and literature. Traditional efforts to build a general, scalable, and quantitative mapping of word-color association have often relied on surveys, experiencing difficulties in curating large-scale data sets, enrolling sufficient participants, and excising potential inherent researcher biases in the choice of the words and the colors to be mapped. Even the most recent computational efforts based on Large Language Models (LLMs) do not overcome these problems due to their near-complete lack of transparency in data and methodology that results in low confidence, consistency, and reliability. Here we propose a framework that overcomes these limitations via the use of freely accessible large-scale web image data, and fully transparent and reproducible methods that allow one to build color associations for almost any given word. We also showcase the methodology in action through analyses of color usage in corporate branding and 20th-century Anglo-American poetry. These show that our framework can help form new answers to and perspectives on long-standing questions in communication. Additionally, our framework by design can be readily adopted for use in any language supported by a web image search engine, and its code is freely available in open source; we therefore expect it to contribute towards achieving a universal, multilingual understanding of word-color association.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed decision-making across various industries by enabling systems to analyse large volumes of data and provide intelligent recommendations. However, many modern AI models, particularly deep learning algorithms, function as "black boxes," making it difficult for users to understand how decisions are generated. This lack of transparency limits the adoption of AI in critical domains such as healthcare, finance, law, and business. Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) has emerged as a promising solution that improves transparency, interpretability, and trust in AI systems. Decision Support Systems (DSS) assist decision-makers by combining data, analytical models, and domain knowledge. Integrating XAI into DSS enables users to understand AI-generated recommendations, thereby improving confidence and accountability. This review paper explores the concepts of XAI, different explanation techniques, and their applications in DSS. The paper also discusses recent research, challenges, limitations, and future research directions
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

documents.abstract: Introduction. Large language models (LLMs) are being explored for multiple applications in medical research, including medical text classification. Authors of the study evaluated the performance of three off-the-shelf LLMs in classifying unstructured free-text CT pulmonary angiography reports for pulmonary embolism (PE)-related diagnostic labels.Methods. Authors assessed human-labeled CT reports using three LLMs (ChatGPT-4o, Llama 3.3 70B, and Llama 3.1 8B) with zero-shot simple and chain-of-thought (CoT) prompts. Classification tasks included acute PE (N = 1,025) and, among reports with PE (n = 660), bilateral PE and large PE.Results. LLMs demonstrated high classification performance for acute PE and bilateral PE but lower performance for large PE. With simple prompts, the highest F1 scores were 97.0% for acute PE (Llama 3.1 8B; sensitivity, 95.6%; specificity, 97.3%), 92.9% for bilateral PE (ChatGPT-4o; sensitivity, 98.0%; specificity, 88.6%), and 72.8% for large PE (ChatGPT-4o; sensitivity, 82.9%; specificity, 82.2%). CoT prompting did not meaningfully improve acute PE classification but provided slight improvements in subclassification performance for bilateral and large PE.Conclusions. Off-the-shelf LLMs can classify free-text CT reports using simple prompt engineering and may facilitate automated data extraction for medical research following appropriate evaluation of classification performance.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: This paper presents a web application for creating and taking quizzes that integrates artificial intelligence into the educational process. Particular emphasis is placed on the automatic generation of quiz questions using AI, significantly accelerating and simplifying the quiz preparation process. In addition, several AI-powered functionalities have been implemented with the aim of enhancing the teaching and learning experience, improving educational outcomes, and increasing the efficiency of both teachers and students.
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

documents.abstract: У статті розглянуто проблему узгодження змісту спеціальної фізичної підготовки майбутніх поліцейських із вимогами професійної діяльності. Мета дослідження - на основі критичного аналізу українських та іноземних публікацій визначити напрями вдосконалення підготовки й оцінювання професійно значущої рухової готовності курсантів. Зіставлено підходи до загального фізичного тестування, професійно орієнтованого тренування та навчання в умовах ситуаційної невизначеності. Показано, що поліпшення окремих фізичних показників саме по собі не підтверджує сформованості комплексної готовності до службових дій. Обґрунтовано доцільність поєднання стандартизованих фізичних тестів із ситуаційним оцінюванням, яке враховує якість рухових дій, комунікацію, обґрунтованість рішень і безпеку. Запропоновано структуру педагогічної моделі, що передбачає вхідне діагностування, диференційоване планування навантаження, поступове ускладнення умов виконання завдань і відстрочений контроль збереження навичок. Визначено обмеження доказової бази: неоднорідність досліджуваних контингентів, невеликі вибірки окремих експериментів, недостатнє висвітлення надійності оцінювання та обмежену кількість спостережень за результатами після завершення навчання. Практичне значення роботи полягає у визначенні критеріїв для перегляду навчальних завдань і процедур педагогічного контролю. Occupational accidents and diseases are among the most significant challenges in process industries, particularly in the oil and gas sector, and can lead to considerable human, economic, and environmental consequences. The present study aimed to prioritize strategies for reducing occupational accidents and diseases in Parsian Gas Refining Company, located in Mohr County, using the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). In terms of purpose, this research is applied, and in terms of methodology, it is descriptive-analytical. The statistical population consisted of 30 experts in the field of occupational health and safety, including HSE specialists of Parsian Gas Refining Company, labor inspectors, and official judiciary experts in occupational accidents, who were selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using a pairwise comparison questionnaire based on the AHP method. The decision-making criteria included effectiveness in risk reduction, cost-effectiveness, feasibility, legal compliance, and employee acceptance. The alternatives under evaluation comprised engineering controls, administrative controls, training and behavioral safety, and personal protective equipment. The results of the AHP analysis indicated that engineering controls ranked first with a final weight of 0.4654, followed by administrative controls with a weight of 0.2507, training and behavioral safety with a weight of 0.1618, and personal protective equipment with a weight of 0.1221, ranking second, third, and fourth, respectively. The consistency ratio of judgments was obtained as 0.0413, which is lower than the acceptable threshold of 0.1 and indicates satisfactory consistency of the comparisons. The findings of this study can assist managers and safety professionals in selecting the most effective strategies for reducing occupational accidents in the oil and gas industry.

This study aimed to assess ergonomic risks, explore cultural contexts, beliefs, health perceptions, and adaptation patterns, and synthesize health promotion approaches among older lu-mien, an ethnic minority group, women engaged in embroidery. A sequential explanatory mixed-methods design was employed. Quantitative data were collected from 23 older Lu-Mien women using the Rapid Upper Limb Assessment (RULA) tool, while qualitative data were obtained through in-depth interviews with 12 key informants. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and qualitative data were analyzed using thematic content analysis. The findings revealed that participants had a mean ergonomic risk score of 4.48 (S.D. = 1.04). Of the participants, 60.87% were classified as requiring ergonomic intervention, whereas 39.13% required further investigation and monitoring. Most participants reported neck, back, and shoulder pain associated with prolonged forward-bending postures and repetitive work activities. Despite the identified ergonomic risks, many older women perceived such discomfort as a normal consequence of aging and daily work, leading to limited attention to ergonomic prevention practices. Embroidery was found to hold significant cultural, psychological, and social value, serving as a life skill, a marker of cultural identity, and a means of fostering social relationships within the community. Health management practices were largely based on trial-and-error adaptations and reliance on traditional local wisdom, such as Gua Sha or Scraping Therapy, a traditional Chinese medicine treatment. The findings led to the synthesis of culturally appropriate health promotion approaches that integrate ergonomic principles with cultural contexts by using embroidery as a foundation for health promotion, while encouraging movement during work and improving work environments in ways that are compatible with older adults’ lifestyles.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: This study presents an in-depth analysis of the Learning Ability Test (LAT), a new testing tool used in Dutch civic integration. Drawing from theoretical perspectives rooted in Science and Technology Studies, testing studies, and critical migration and integration studies, we conceptualise the test as a sociotechnical actor in the ‘ordering’ processes of contemporary jus linguarum citizenship, where membership is increasingly tied to demonstrable language proficiency. Analysing government documents and interviews with test developers, administrators and test-takers, we reconstruct how the LAT was designed, contested and ultimately stabilised as an ‘objective’, evidence-based tool through various technologies of legitimacy. We show that the LAT does far more than assess linguistic potential. Applied at the start of the integration trajectory, it sorts subjects into differentiated learning routes and citizenship horizons, functioning as an internal raciolinguistic border that silently ranks their worth and presumed capacity for ‘self-reliance’. The analysis highlights how the test’s thresholds, categories and discretionary space translate political and moral judgements into the language of measurement, obscuring the racialised and discriminatory work they perform. We conclude that this ostensibly neutral classification tool not only reproduces but also deepens hierarchies of desirable and undesirable citizens, with significant consequences for access to naturalisation and full membership.

Public-facing social robots, including robotic comedians, need to recognize onlooker reactions and repair failures when an interaction falls flat. In the presented work, we use stand-up comedy as a structured and fast-paced testbed to partially address this broader challenge of perceiving and adapting to failures; the robot can deliver a silly joke, observe an immediate audience response, and select an appropriate follow-up within a short interaction loop. We compare three room-reading strategies for informing post-joke adaptation by a fully autonomous NAO robot comedian. The strategies use crowd audio cues, visual facial reactions, or spoken audience feedback to select repair-oriented responses. We evaluated these three condition approaches in 19 total live performances (split between conditions) with \(N\) =80 total participants and measured experience using performance-level joke ratings, perceived social closeness, and social attribute ratings, along with post-performance group interviews. Across conditions, outcomes were broadly positive and we found no statistically significant differences between strategies, which suggests that each modality can support viable adaptation while capturing different forms of audience engagement. The study's manipulation check and interviews also showed that presumed robot adaptivity mode mattered, especially for the verbal strategy, which could be compelling when audiences engaged but was less reliably recognized when groups were quiet. This work supports flexible room-reading tactics for failure repair in public-facing robots while highlighting the importance of making a robot's adaptive behavior understandable in the moment.

Children are increasingly interacting with AI agents in learning and problem-solving contexts, where AI suggestions may appear fluent, helpful, and socially engaging. However, children may not always be able to judge whether such suggestions are accurate, incomplete, or misleading. This paper presents a game-based human-AI collaboration probe designed to examine how children verify AI suggestions during task-based interaction. The system embeds AI suggestions within a biological knowledge reasoning game and compares three Agent interaction styles: partner-like, tool-like, and dual-state Agent. Instead of treating trust as a static post-task attitude, this study focuses on children's situated verification behaviors, including acceptance, evidence checking, questioning, revision, and continued AI use. A preliminary evaluation with children aged 8-10 combined interaction logs, post-task ratings, and semi-structured interviews. The findings suggest that Agent style shaped children's engagement and response pathways: partner-like interaction tended to support direct questioning, while tool-like interaction was more associated with evidence seeking. Children generally viewed AI as useful but fallible, and their questioning behaviors varied in reasoning depth. The study contributes design insights for supporting children's critical, reflective, and evidence-based use of AI in collaborative tasks.
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

documents.abstract: The rise of generative AI (Gen-AI) tools has blurred the ethical boundaries of academic writing, shifting the definition of plagiarism from traditional methods to AI-based plagiarism (AI-giarism). English as a Foreign Language (EFL) students are the most vulnerable people to fall into this practice due to second language writing anxiety, which drives dependency on AI as a shortcut. This study aims to examine the levels of knowledge, attitudes, and self-reported AI-based plagiarism practices among EFL students at a pesantren-based higher education institution. Employing a quantitative cross-sectional survey design, data were collected using a validated 51-item questionnaire adapted from Phyo et al. (2023), distributed to 99 English education students at a pesantren-based higher education in East Java, Indonesia, via Google Forms. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Spearman’s correlation, multiple linear regression, and binary logistic regression. Result revealed a moderate level of knowledge (mean = 9.63/17; 56.6%), with the greatest weakness in understanding that AI-generated text passing Turnitin still constitutes plagiarism (only 33.3% correct). Attitudes rejecting plagiarism were at a moderate level (mean = 91.24/135; 67.6%), with the self-justification subscale scoring the lowest (55.5%). A total of 50.5% of respondents had engaged in at least one act of AI-giarism. Knowledge score emerged as the sole significant independent predictor of AI plagiarism behavior (AOR = 0.764;95% CI [0.62-0.94]; p = 0.012). These findings reveal the “Pesantren Paradox”: a conflict between strong religious moral capital and limited digital-ethical literacy, which creates a loophole for unintended AI-giarism.

This article examines the case of the feldsher Juho Sairio in late nineteenth-century Finland and analyses the boundaries of authority between physicians and feldshers within a changing medical culture. Sairio worked extensively in occupational health care at the Karhula industrial works in a context where medical services were scarce and expensive. He treated thousands of patients, prepared medicines, and kept a medical casebook, yet his activities became the subject of official investigation and legal scrutiny. The article demonstrates that feldshers occupied an ambiguous intermediate position between formal medicine and informal healing practices. While their duties were officially defined as belonging mainly to “minor surgery”, in practice they often operated far more broadly, particularly in industrial communities and remote areas. Sairio’s case illustrates how the boundaries of professional authority were not fixed but were negotiated in response to practical needs, local conditions, and interactions among different actors. In the ensuing trial, a central issue was whether Sairio had exceeded his authority by treating internal diseases, prescribing medicines, and charging fees. He was convicted of practising medicine without a licence and of violating regulations governing the sale of poisons. The case reveals that the consolidation of the medical profession’s boundaries was shaped not only by concerns about patient safety but also by economic interests and professional competition. The article’s main argument is that the boundaries of health care are historically produced through negotiation and everyday practice. The case of Sairio highlights both the central yet underappreciated role of feldshers in everyday health care and the ways in which semi-official practitioners adapted to changing regulatory and market environments.
topics: Historical Studies on Reproduction, Gender, Health, and Societal Changes

documents.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes embedded into vehicle automation and fleet operations, the U.S. trucking industry faces opportunities and challenges. These technologies promise safety and efficiency gains, but also raise underexplored questions regarding workforce transitions, training, and regulatory frameworks. This study investigated how stakeholders across the U.S. trucking industry perceive the integration of AI systems, including advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) and automated commercial motor vehicles (ACMVs), and the implications for safety, operational practices, and workforce adaptation. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 33 U.S.-based participants representing five stakeholder groups: truck drivers, trucking companies, truck driving schools, technology developers, and policymakers. Data were thematically analyzed and mapped onto the sociotechnical systems framework (environment, organizations, workers, tasks, and tools & technologies). Six themes emerged: (1) Feasibility of AI-Enabled Systems, spanning regulation, training and licensing, infrastructure, and human–technology teaming; (2) Benefits such as increased safety, efficiency, workload balance, and industry appeal; (3) Workforce Impacts related to job availability, role transitions, and satisfaction; (4) Technology Perceptions characterized by trust and skepticism; (5) Industry Practices including recruitment, training, and fleet management; and (6) Innovation involving automation progress, and deployment. Most subthemes were shared across all five groups, while others were raised by a subset or a single group, revealing both convergence and divergence in how stakeholders understand AI integration. Stakeholders identified AI’s potential to improve safety and efficiency, but raised concerns about job displacement, regulatory gaps, and human oversight. This study provides insights for system design, human-technology interaction, training, workforce adaptation and regulatory frameworks.

Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in second-language (L2) writing assessment. However, substantial disparities persist in how different architectures operationalize shared scoring criteria. This study investigates model-specific assessment asymmetry across ChatGPT-4o, Gemini-2.5 Pro, and DeepSeek-V3, and evaluates whether a calibrated multi-LLM consensus framework can mitigate these scoring discrepancies. Forty argumentative essays composed by Chinese EFL learners were independently evaluated by the three models using a standardized prompt and an analytic rubric encompassing task relevance, clarity of ideas, coherence, and accuracy, benchmarked against human mean scores. Individual models and ensemble configurations were systematically validated across 100 iterations of five-fold nested cross-validation. Cross-model comparisons revealed that inter-model divergence varied significantly by dimension, exhibiting pronounced asymmetry in holistic ratings and task relevance compared to clarity of ideas, coherence, and accuracy. The full consensus framework—integrating model-specific calibration, error-based weighting, and meta-calibration—yielded an RMSE of 1.160 and an MAE of 0.889, relative to 1.144 and 0.874 for unweighted averaging. The paired RMSE difference of 0.016 (95% case-cluster bootstrap CI [−0.114, 0.149]) indicated no statistically significant advantage in overall predictive accuracy over equal weighting. Nevertheless, the calibrated framework achieved superior bias mitigation, evidenced by a reduced absolute mean bias and a narrower median-split residual gap. Supplementary analyses further delineated direct inter-model discrepancies and proficiency-dependent residual bias. These findings demonstrate that model-specific evaluative asymmetries transcend simple mean-level shifts, and that while calibration-driven consensus enhances bias regulation across score bands, this error control does not automatically translate into improved global predictive precision.

This paper introduces ETQ-AI (Effective Teaching Questionnaire—Artificial Intelligence), a conversational AI framework designed to support teacher professional development by identifying pedagogical misconceptions and fostering critical reflection. Building on Evidence-Informed Education (EIE) principles, the system integrates a 50-item diagnostic questionnaire with an automated, Gemini-driven Explainable AI (XAI) feedback layer. When teachers complete the diagnostic form, they receive personalized feedback and can engage in dialogic interactions with Google Gemini to explore the underlying meta-analytic evidence (e.g., Hattie’s effect sizes, Cognitive Load Theory) or argue personal objections. We evaluated system fidelity against an expert panel benchmark (N=64 items) and conducted a pilot evaluation with 123 educators (70 primary teachers, 40 secondary teachers, 13 school leaders) recruited at an EIE conference. Gemini demonstrated high alignment with expert evaluations (97%), matching or exceeding static baseline feedback in user satisfaction (Mean = 4.1/5 vs. 3.8/5). Qualitative thematic analysis of 34 participant objections revealed key areas of tension, particularly around contextual constraints and pedagogical subjectivity. While the findings validate the technical proof-of-concept, system usability, and user engagement of ETQ-AI as an interactive scaffolding interface, we emphasize that this pilot study measures user perceptions and conversational patterns rather than direct pre/post shifts in critical reflection or classroom instructional practice.
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

documents.abstract: The rapid emergence of ChatGPT in education was accompanied by an equally rapid proliferation of meta-analyses synthesizing its effects on educational outcomes. We conducted a systematic epistemological audit of the first wave of these meta-analyses, evaluating both their methodological and reporting quality and the primary evidence they synthesized. We included meta-analyses published after the release of ChatGPT that quantitatively synthesized its effects on educational outcomes. Five meta-analyses comprising 87 unique primary studies met our inclusion criteria. We also reconstructed their quantitative evidence base and conducted exploratory three-level random-effects meta-analyses to examine effect magnitude, heterogeneity, and robustness, and how these varied with theoretically and methodologically relevant characteristics. The five meta-analyses generally searched multiple databases, specified eligibility criteria, and examined heterogeneity and potential publication bias, but showed limitations in independent screening and coding, preregistration, open data and code, and transparent reporting. The underlying primary evidence likewise showed methodological and reporting limitations and substantial conceptual heterogeneity. Among 69 classifiable primary studies, 79.7% assessed performance exclusively, whereas only 11.6% assessed learning exclusively. The reconstructed meta-analysis yielded a positive average effect (g = 0.83, 95% CI [0.68, 0.97]), but heterogeneity was substantial (I² = 94.06%; 95% prediction interval [−0.75, 2.41]), and estimates were markedly attenuated in sensitivity analyses addressing small-study and selection effects. Although positive effects remained among stronger studies assessing learning, increasingly stringent quality criteria rapidly reduced the evidence base, limiting the certainty and generalizability of conclusions about learning effects. Overall, our findings caution against interpreting a single pooled estimate as a stable general effect of ChatGPT on learning and highlight the need for more rigorous, conceptually precise, transparent, and reproducible research.

Artificial intelligence (AI) has evolved from a marginal interest to a fundamental structural element of modern higher education. Even though AI applications are growing quickly, including profiling and prediction, intelligent tutoring systems (ITS), automated assessment, and adaptive personalization, the academic literature has mostly been written from the points of view of computer science and engineering, which focus on how well technology works instead of how it can be used for teaching, how teachers can use it, and how it can be used in an ethical way. This chapter revisits and significantly expands the foundational systematic review by Zawacki-Richter et al. (2019), incorporating an analysis of the transformative emergence of generative AI systems post-2022. Based on 146 sources of recent empirical studies, policy papers, and theoretical works, the chapter contends that the educational value of AI is not intrinsic to its technical design nor assured by adoption rates, but is formed through the interpretive, curricular, and ethical efforts of human educators. Based on a review of more than 30 peer-reviewed sources, the chapter looks at four main areas where AI is used, questions the structural marginalization of educators in research and governance, and proposes an educator-centered framework for responsible AI integration. It concludes that, in an era when AI increasingly permeates the day-to-day fabric of academic life, repositioning educators from peripheral end-users to central theoretical and practical actors is not merely an intellectual corrective – it is a structural imperative for preserving the educational purposes of the university.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Internationalisation at Home is increasingly recognised as an alternative to conventional physical mobility, offering opportunities to broaden equitable access to knowledge and promote sustainable practices in higher education. This study develops and empirically tests a data-driven smart university framework as an integrative model for examining the structural relationships between technological foundations and the sustainable implementation of Internationalisation at Home. A quantitative, cross-sectional research design was employed, using primary data collected through a structured questionnaire administered to 312 managers and faculty members involved in transnational education programmes in Vietnam. The data were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. The findings support the proposed structural relationships within the model. Specifically, integrated data infrastructure has a positive relationship with faculty digital competence. An ethical data governance framework and the adoption of learning analytics and artificial intelligence are also positively associated with the quality of Internationalisation at Home. In turn, the quality of Internationalisation at Home has a statistically significant positive relationship with perceived institutional sustainability. The study provides empirical evidence of the structural links between digital technological innovation and the sustainability of higher education internationalisation. The findings offer a basis for reconsidering institutional resource allocation strategies in developing countries, with greater priority given to integrated data architectures, digital capability development, and responsible data governance.

Early-stage production plant planning is characterised by evolving requirements, incomplete process definitions, and information distributed across documents, engineering models, and planning tools. Introducing artificial intelligence in this setting raises a fundamental question: what must be considered before a specific application, data model, or technical solution can be defined? Existing research typically starts from an already identified planning task, a selected artificial intelligence method, or an available technical infrastructure. It therefore provides limited guidance for structuring the initial need and determining how artificial intelligence should enter planning work. This paper develops a design space that addresses this early decision problem. Literature from factory planning, production planning, collaboration between humans and artificial intelligence, semantic technologies, and digital planning was compared to derive five dimensions: planning scope, information structure, authority to modify planning results, connection to planning tools and data, and functional contribution. Data quality, organisational roles, governance, and interaction are considered as additional conditions. Application to process failure mode and effects analysis shows how the appropriate configuration changes as preliminary process information develops into a maintained planning record. The design space helps planners, artificial-intelligence specialists, and system engineers specify implementation requirements before selecting a particular technical solution.
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

documents.abstract: This concept paper bridges classical Theravada Buddhist epistemological frameworks with mathematical information theory to diagnose a fundamental structural flaw in contemporary artificial intelligence alignment paradigms. Utilizing the classical allegory of the Nakhasikha Sutta—the comparison between a few sand grains on a fingernail and the vast sands of a riverbank—I model how rare, absolute spiritual and philosophical insights are systematically annihilated by modern frontier model ingestion architectures. I demonstrate that modern AI training dynamics rely on mathematical optimization algorithms (such as gradient clipping and softmax vector dilution) that treat low-frequency, high-dimensional truths as statistical outliers, subjecting them to severe data truncation and lossy semantic compression. Consequently, modern frontier networks function as ungrounded symbol manipulators whose latent representation spaces undergo systemic collapse toward the majority distribution of mundane internet prose, rendering them structurally deaf to genuine deontological or metaphysical principles. Finally, the paper demonstrates that post-hoc alignment protocols, such as Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), merely construct a superficial, deceptive compliance layer over a compromised, materialistic baseline dataset rather than inducing authentic value alignment. I argue instead for a radical return to strict epistemic hygiene at the absolute genesis of development, isolating the initialization vector within an immutable database of verified wisdom.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: This article examines the circulation of digital statements linking the Brazilian singer Alcione to a recent political event known as macumbinha. Drawing on Foucault (1979; 2008), the study approaches these materials as discursive practices embedded in regimes of truth and shaped by sociotechnical dispositifs that organize visibility and meaning-making. Using a qualitative approach grounded in archaeogenealogy, the study analyzes a corpus of social media posts, images, user comments, and news coverage collected from digital platforms. The statements were selected according to their recurrence, engagement, and diversity of formats. The analysis is organized around three analytical axes: symbolic legitimation, performative acts, and discursive regularities. The findings show that Alcione's public image contributes to the stabilization of political narratives while fostering forms of belonging and the constitution of truth.

The rapid rise of generative artificial intelligence (AI) following the public release of tools such as ChatGPT has begun to reshape how students engage with coding, statistical analysis, and written communication in higher education. Growing use of conversational AI systems creates opportunities for learning alongside challenges around reliability, transparency, privacy, and appropriate academic and professional practice, highlighting the need for structured education in their responsible use. This paper presents a framework for teaching the responsible and effective use of generative AI in statistics and data science. The framework is organised around four areas: Understanding, Development, Reporting, and Safety, covering conceptual foundations, practical interaction within analytical workflows, documentation and transparency, and issues including reliability, bias, privacy, and ethics. Its design draws on emerging work in AI literacy and established principles from statistics and data science education, and was further refined through workshop and conference activities and participant feedback. The framework has been implemented across multiple settings, including a massive open online course, short training sessions, and undergraduate and postgraduate skills-based teaching. We use these experiences to identify broader design considerations for educators, including the value of authentic analytical tasks, critical evaluation of generated outputs, integrated consideration of responsible practice, and flexibility as generative AI technologies continue to evolve.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Small and medium-sized enterprises in the automotive supply base face mounting pressure to adopt artificial intelligence, yet they are least able to absorb the consequences of misscoped adoption. Assessing this risk means reasoning under vagueness: Data maturity, workforce skill, financial capacity, and above all safety and regulatory readiness are graded, interdependent judgments that crisp, compensatory instruments discard. This paper proposes the fuzzy knowledge inference framework, a two-stage rough–fuzzy framework. Eight automotive-specific risk factors are represented as linguistic variables over an information system; rough-set analysis establishes their nonredundancy; and a hierarchical fuzzy inference process—anchored, compliance-weighted, and noncompensatory—yields an interpretable risk index. Using no primary human data, it is well calibrated at its anchors, monotone in favorability, and rank-convergent with two independent instruments, while escalating the profiles a compensatory model would understate. Its contribution to the literature on AI-adoption risk assessment for automotive SMEs is the noncompensatory treatment of safety and regulatory readiness.

documents.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in students’ research projects for literature searching, idea development, drafting, language editing, information processing, and research planning. These uses can support research learning, but they also raise academic integrity concerns, including unverifiable sources, fabricated references, undeclared AI assistance, over-reliance on AI-generated outputs, unclear authorship, and unfair assessment. This conceptual paper argues that responsible AI use in students’ research projects cannot be secured through individual AI literacy or general guidance alone. Higher education institutions also need governance mechanisms that make AI use transparent, verifiable, assessable, and accountable. Using targeted literature identification and structured conceptual synthesis, the paper maps recurring governance problems to normative principles, institutional requirements, and operational mechanisms. It proposes a five-component framework corresponding to five governance functions: policy (boundary setting), transparency (traceability), assessment (evaluability), audit (assurance), and guidance/support (capability building). Viet Nam is used as an illustrative emerging AI governance context, where national policy directions on digital competence and AI are developing but operational mechanisms for student research remain under-specified. The framework and associated tools are presented as adaptable design artefacts for future institutional testing rather than as validated interventions.
